title: Beyond Fidelity: Resolving Errors in Photonic Seed State Generation
authors: Sara Bartolucci, Patrick Birchall, Jacob Bulmer, Sam Gartenstein, Mihir Pant, Terry Rudolph, Chris Sparrow, Andrzej Veitia
abstract: An important aspect of many linear optical quantum computing architectures is probabilistically generating small dual-rail qubit entangled states, or seed states. While many schemes to achieve this have been discovered, attention has been primarily focused on minimizing input resources and maximizing success probability rather than establishing a detailed understanding of linear-optical error performance. In this work, we develop a framework for resolving sensitivities to physically distinct errors in linear optical state generation, allowing us to identify precise ways in which these errors affect the properties of the output state. We use this framework to identify seed state generators in which destructive many-photon interference prevents detector loss and detector noise from causing a falsely successful heralding event. We show that this effect suppresses errors, for example cutting the effective loss on the output of particular Bell state generators in half relative to a standard scheme. We also present a new Bell state generator in which both detector loss and detector noise do not affect the quality of the output Bell state to first order, and a 4GHZ generator with >75% higher success probability than a standard circuit. In addition we provide some useful identities, bounds and invariants for studying linear optical seed state generation.
summary: This paper introduces a detailed error analysis framework for generating entangled photonic seed states crucial for linear optical quantum computing. By moving beyond simple fidelity metrics, the authors quantify how specific detector losses and noise channels degrade the output state. They demonstrate improved generators that are robust to these common physical imperfections.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for a detailed understanding of linear-optical error performance when probabilistically generating entangled seed states for quantum computing.
main_result: The authors developed a framework showing that destructive many-photon interference can suppress errors, and they presented new generators where detector loss and noise do not affect the output Bell state quality to first order.
method: They developed a comprehensive framework to resolve sensitivities to physically distinct errors, analyzing the output state's probability distribution over error-affected subspaces rather than just fidelity.
model_or_system: The work focuses on photonic quantum computing architectures utilizing linear optical transformations to generate small dual-rail qubit entangled states (seed states). The analysis models errors arising from input channels and detector measurements.
key_observables: The conditional heralded subspace probability distribution $	ext{Pr}(Q|p)$ and the error response coefficients $c(p)$ are key observables.
important_parameters: The analysis is performed to first order in the error probability $ eta_E$, and the success probability of the generators is a key metric.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that errors are single-mode error channels applied sequentially (input or detector) and neglects errors occurring within the interferometer components.
figures_summary: The notes reference tables detailing error response coefficients for various generators (S6, H8, etc.) across different Pauli error combinations, and figures illustrating error mechanisms.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops an error framework, applies it to analyze specific seed state generators (Bell and GHZ states), and quantifies the error response coefficients for various error channels.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it provides rigorous, quantitative tools to characterize and mitigate realistic noise sources (detector loss/noise) in photonic quantum computation protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic for the error mechanisms that we consider in this work. Distinguishability, multiphoton (coherent photon addition), and loss at the input, and loss and detector noise (incoherent photon addition) at the detectors. Yellow circles are photons in the “good” mode, red circles are photons in the “bad” mode. Here shown as an example for some ninp = m = 5 Bell state generation circuit, e.g. the 5DFT in Figure 4a. These error mechanisms lead to a noisy output state, ρ(p) out, which we can then use to calculate output subspace probabilities Pr(Q|p) as discussed in Section III B.

FIG. 2. Commuting of the loss channels at the input to loss channels on the SSG output modes. The quantities next to the ellipses give the probability which parameterizes the loss channel, as defined in Appendix B. The first step shows how the balanced loss channels commute across a unitary matrix to loss channels on the output and detected modes, while the second step shows the transformation of loss on the detected mode to effective loss on the SSG outputs. The resulting effective loss can be seen to be minimized when the error response coefficient cLdet→QV = 0. The remainder of the loss on the outputs is unavoidable.

FIG. 3. Sketch of the error processes which should be considered to model detector loss and detector noise, with Kraus operators as defined in Appendix B. In this example, the S6 Bell state generator, introduced in Section VI C with a successful detection outcome p = (2, 2), is drawn. When loss and multiphoton errors are commuted through the circuit, the intrinsic error removal properties of the S6 SSG mean that there is zero amplitude for any output where the states |2⟩|3⟩, |3⟩|2⟩, |1⟩|2⟩, or |2⟩|1⟩are present in the two detected modes. Thus, when we condition on the successful measurement outcome, to first order there is no impact from these error channels.

FIG. 4. Circuit schematic of seed state generators discussed in Section VI. The 5DFT (a), 2-3DFT (b), S6 (c), and H8 (d) Bell state generator circuits, the 2-H4 3GHZ state generator circuit (e) and the 4-3DFT 4GHZ state generator circuit (f). Black horizontal and crossing lines represent optical modes. Rounded boxes indicate any implementation of the indicated unitary transformation. Black vertical lines indicate balanced beam splitters, with transformation given by H. Triangles are passive phase shifts. Circuit layouts are drawn with detectors on the first mdet modes. FIG. 5. Certain error mechanisms in SSG produce states in which multiple qubits are simultaneously in leakage subspaces. Such leakage is likely to cause subsequent fusions to fail, preventing the affected states from entering the resource state. We call these errors fusion heraldable. Panel (a) sketches one way in which these fusion heraldable states can be generated. Here detector loss in the 2-H4 3GHZ generator results in a state which lives in the (M, V, V ), (V, M, V ), or (V, V, M) output subspaces.
